'''Raymond Daudel''' (2 February 1920<ref name=INT>[http://www.quantum-chemistry-history.com/Daudel1.htm An interview with Raymond Daudel]</ref><ref name=IAQMS>[http://www.quantum-chemistry-history.com/Daud_Dat/DaudelRa.htm His International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science page]</ref><ref name=PPT>[http://www.lcpmr.upmc.fr/Daudel_Obit.pdf Obituary by Jean Maruani] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061124080551/http://www.lcpmr.upmc.fr/Daudel_Obit.pdf |date=2006-11-24 }}</ref> – 20 June 2006<ref name=PPT/>) was a French [[theoretical chemistry|theoretical]] and [[Quantum chemistry|quantum chemist]].

Trained as a physicist, he was an assistant to [[Irène Joliot-Curie]] at the [[Curie Institute (Paris)|Radium Institute]].<ref name=INT/> Daudel spent almost the entirety of his career as professor at the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]] and director of a laboratory of the [[Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]] (CNRS). He is quoted as saying that the latter "was much better because the CNRS was very rich".<ref name=INT/> This allowed Daudel to attract many co-workers from elsewhere in France and internationally.

Raymond Daudel was ''Officier de la [[Légion d'honneur]]'' and ''Officier de l'[[Ordre National du Mérite]]''.<ref name=IAQMS/> He served as President of the [[European Academy of Arts Sciences and Humanities]],<ref name=IAQMS/> in Paris, France. Daudel was a founding member and Honorary President of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]].<ref name=PPT/>

An author as well as an academic, Raymond Daudel authored several books, including ''Quantum chemistry'', originally with R. Lefebyre and C. Moser in 1959 (Interscience Publishers, Inc., New York) and later with G. Leroy, D. Peeters, and M. Sana, published by Wiley in 1983.<ref name=IAQMS/> He was responsible for the organization of the first International Congress in [[Quantum chemistry|Quantum Chemistry]], held in [[Menton]], France in 1973.
